summary: The group-007 source dossier covering Kuhn sections 9.1-9.5 (philosophical, neurobiological, electromagnetic-field, computational/informational, and homeostatic/affective materialism) is factual NotebookLM source material, not a performed script. It preserves the hard-problem audit, distinguishes target phenomena and bridge relations, uses prior course continuity only as framing, and epistemically tags claims as mainstream scientific theory, active philosophical debate, speculative extension, or weakly evidenced. Strongest objections are preserved per section and consolidated in the limits section. Major claims trace to the cited literature (Kuhn 2024, Stoljar SEP, Place/Smart, Churchland, Papineau, Chalmers, Jackson, Nagel, Levine, Bourget & Chalmers PhilPapers 2020, Seth & Bayne, Koch et al., Crick & Koch, Dehaene & Naccache, Casali et al., Doerig et al., Cogitate 2025, Buzsaki/Anastassiou/Koch, Frohlich & McCormick, Anastassiou et al., McFadden, Pockett, Turing, Searle, Block, Piccinini & Scarantino, Grossberg, Butlin et al., Friston, Seth, Barrett & Simmons, Damasio, Solms, LeDoux & Brown, Williams). Speculative extensions (AI consciousness, uploading, survival, cosmic EM) are flagged and not asserted. Suitable to become durable course continuity.
non_blocking_notes: The 'Source Notes' section enumerates a few authors as cluster anchors that lack full bibliographic entries in the citations array (e.g., Rodriguez et al. on long-distance synchronization, Pinotsis & Miller on stable working-memory fields, Xu et al. on spiral waves, Kleckner et al. on allostatic-interoceptive networks, Aru et al. on distilling NCCs, Storm et al. on multiscale neural theories, Hesse & Gross / Toker et al. on criticality, Hunt and Jones on EM-field theories, Barrett on constructed emotion, Panksepp on affective consciousness, Nave et al. on predictive processing). The substantive claims those names support are independently backed by other cited works, but traceability would be tighter if these were either added to the citations array with DOIs or removed from the source notes.

The PhilPapers 2020 figures are stated to two decimal places (51.93% physicalism, 32.08% non-physicalism). The cited Bourget & Chalmers source supports the general finding that physicalism leads but is not consensus; the precise percentages should be sanity-checked against the survey results page on a future pass.

The dossier briefly says 'Edelman's reentry and dynamic core, ... Dennett's multiple drafts model, Minsky's society of mind, ... Northoff's temporo-spatial approach, Bunge's emergent materialism' inside section 9.2 without anchoring each to a citation. The family list is accurate, but if any of these names is reused as evidence in later episodes the capsule should attach explicit references.
checked_items: Source script JSON and dossier markdown are present, identical in content, and structurally coherent.
Dossier is structured factual material with sections, verdict matrix, and comparison axes; no host dialogue, speaker labels, stage directions, banter, or performed narration.
Course continuity grounding section explicitly limits prior episodes to framing and pacing, with current research records and packet inputs as the factual sources.

Epistemic discipline applied: each section closes with an 'Epistemic status' label using the contract's categories (mainstream scientific theory, active philosophical debate, speculative extension, weakly evidenced); dedicated 'Epistemic Status And What Not To Overstate' section enforces the same.
Bridge relations (identity, realization, constitution, causal enabling, correlation, organizational invariance, etc.) are named per theory family and separated from explanation.

Major claims are traceable to a sizable citations array including Kuhn 2024, SEP entries, the canonical hard-problem and identity-theory literature, the 2025 Cogitate adversarial collaboration, ephaptic-coupling and field-origin papers, computational and AI-indicator literature, and homeostatic/interoception/active-inference sources.
Speculative extensions (AI consciousness, uploading, survival beyond death, cosmic EM consciousness, paranormal cognition) are explicitly flagged as not established by this cluster's sources.

Serious objections preserved per section (hard problem, explanatory gap, Mary, bat, zombies, multiple realizability, absent/inverted qualia, Chinese Room, China-brain, FEP overbreadth, LeDoux/Brown higher-order challenge to affect-first theories) and consolidated in the seven-limit summary.

Global 'Do Not Overstate' clauses from the course contract are honored (NCCs do not solve the hard problem; formal vocabulary is not empirical confirmation; metaphysical breadth is not explanatory success; popularity does not settle truth).
NotebookLM bundle directory contains research_dossier.md plus all five section sources (six-file handoff).
